name: Centro Storico (San Michele)
tagline: The walled heart around San Michele
description: The core of the walled old town, centred on the church of San Michele in Foro and its lively square. Cobbled lanes, shops, cafes, and history surround you, and everything is a flat, easy walk or cycle away in minutes.
bestFor: Nomads who want history, walkability, and cafes right on the doorstep
pros: Right in the beating heart of Lucca
Cafes, shops, and sights all around
cons: Busy and noisy in peak season

name: Piazza dell'Anfiteatro Quarter
tagline: Around the famous oval Roman square
description: The picturesque northern-central pocket wrapped around the oval Piazza dell'Anfiteatro, built on a Roman amphitheatre. Narrow curving streets, characterful buildings, and buzzing terraces make it one of Lucca's most photographed and atmospheric corners to live near.
bestFor: Those wanting a postcard setting with cafes and buzz nearby
pros: One of the most beautiful squares in Tuscany
Terraces, gelato, and life on your doorstep
cons: Very touristy and crowded in summer

name: San Frediano (Northern Old Town)
tagline: Quieter northern corner within the walls
description: The calmer northern stretch of the walled centre around the basilica of San Frediano, close to the walls themselves. It keeps the historic charm and central convenience but feels a touch more residential and relaxed than the busiest tourist squares.
bestFor: People wanting old-town living with a quieter, more local feel
pros: Steps from the walls for walks and rides

name: San Concordio (Outside the Walls)
tagline: Practical residential area beyond the walls
description: A residential district just south of the walls near the train station, San Concordio offers more everyday amenities, larger flats, and lower rents. It is a short cycle into the centre and handy for trains to Pisa and Florence.
bestFor: Budget-minded nomads wanting space, value, and easy train links
pros: More affordable rents and larger flats
Close to the station for regional trains
Quick cycle into the historic centre
cons: Less charm than inside the walls
More traffic and a plainer streetscape
